documents.title: Cardiology Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — Cardiology, regional hospital
Admitted 01/12/2026   Discharged 01/16/2026

Diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure; new heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 35%).

History: 55-year-old with prior left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025 (post-op LVEF 60%), aneurysmal SAH coiled 11/2025, PE 11/2024, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD. About a week of increasing breathlessness, needing two pillows to sleep, and ankle swelling.
Course: chest film with interstitial edema and small effusions. TTE: LVEF 35% with global hypokinesis, no recurrent myxoma. Troponin flat. Coronary CT angiogram: no obstructive coronary artery disease; cardiomyopathy felt to be nonischemic. Diuresed with IV furosemide, then transitioned to oral. Breathing at baseline by day 3.
Discharge creatinine 1.2 (her baseline).

Discharge medications:
- furosemide 40 mg by mouth once daily (NEW)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily
- metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- omeprazole 20 mg daily
- clobetasol ointment as needed
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: 2 g sodium diet, daily weights, call for gain of 3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week.
Follow-up: cardiology clinic in 2-3 weeks with labs; PCP within 1 week.
Cardiology

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge, admitted 1/12-1/16 with acute decompensated HF. New EF 35%, global hypokinesis, coronary CTA without obstructive disease. Started furosemide 40 daily. Summary reviewed.
Her son is staying with her this month; he came today and has taken over the pill box and the daily weights log. She is tired, short of breath on one flight of stairs, sleeping on one pillow again. Ankles better. Had gone back to half days at school the week before admission; out again now.
Med rec with son: furosemide 40 mg daily (new), lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA. The discharge paperwork lists furosemide twice in different places; went through it with them, it is 40 mg once each morning.
Exam: weight down from admission. BP a little above goal. JVP not elevated. Few crackles at the right base, otherwise clear. Heart regular. Trace ankle edema.
A/P
1. HFrEF, new, nonischemic — on furosemide. Daily weights, low-salt diet. Cardiology appt 2/2. BMP today.
2. HTN — slightly high today, cardiology will review meds at their visit.
3. T2DM, ADPKD — BMP.
Extended FMLA paperwork done. RTC after cardiology.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CLINIC — post-hospital follow-up
Date: 02/02/2026
Patient: Valerie Slattery, 55

Seen after discharge 1/16 for acute decompensated heart failure; LVEF 35%, nonischemic by coronary CTA, prior left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025. Since discharge she has felt more tired than she expected. Her son brought the medication list; the furosemide dose is written differently in two places and it is not clear she has been taking it as prescribed.

Medications as brought: furosemide, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 22.
Exam: slightly dyspneic in conversation. Neck veins not distended. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, no murmur. No significant edema.

Labs today: sodium 138, potassium 3.2, creatinine 1.8 (baseline 1.2), BNP 580.

Assessment: HFrEF, euvolemic to slightly dry on exam, with hypokalemia and a creatinine rise on two diuretics.
Plan:
1. Stop hydrochlorothiazide.
2. Furosemide 40 mg once every morning only — written schedule given to her son.
3. Potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
4. Repeat BMP in one week at her PCP's office.
5. Daily weights, sodium restriction. Return in 6-8 weeks.
Cardiology

documents.title: BMP after diuretic change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium back to normal on KCl, creatinine down to 1.3 a week after stopping HCTZ. Copied to cardiology. Portal message sent: keep the current plan, recheck at her visit later this month.

Feels better than a month ago, less tired. One flight of stairs fine. Weights steady on her log. Son went home last week; she fills the pill box on Sundays and he checks in by video. Back to school full time this week.
Meds: furosemide 40 qAM, KCl 20 mEq daily, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: BP better than January. No JVD. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

1. HFrEF — compensated, decompensation resolved. Continue furosemide and lisinopril per cardiology. BMP today.
2. T2DM — A1c today.
3. HTN — better today with volume controlled; continue lisinopril.
4. Health maintenance — screening mammogram due, ordered for March.
RTC 3-4 months.

orders.order: Diagnostic mammogram and left breast ultrasound

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis, compared with 2023-2025. Scattered fibroglandular density. New irregular mass in the left breast, upper outer quadrant, middle depth, not present in 2025. Right breast negative.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 0: Incomplete. New left breast mass; recall for diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound.

documents.title: Mammogram recall
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Valerie about the screening mammogram: a new area in the left breast needs a closer look. Diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound ordered; imaging center has her on 3/17. Mother's history noted. She was calm and asked good questions; will call me after.

reports.text: Left diagnostic mammogram with spot compression views. The irregular mass at 2 o'clock persists with spiculated margins on spot views. No associated calcifications. No other findings.
reports.conclusion: Persistent irregular spiculated left breast mass at 2 o'clock, highly suggestive of malignancy. BI-RADS 5.

reports.text: Targeted left breast ultrasound. At 2 o'clock, 6 cm from the nipple: irregular hypoechoic mass with angular margins, 2.3 cm in greatest dimension, corresponding to the mammographic finding. Left axilla: normal lymph nodes with fatty hila.
reports.conclusion: 2.3 cm irregular left breast mass at 2 o'clock, BI-RADS 5. Normal left axilla. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy recommended.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of breast
conditions.note: left breast, invasive ductal carcinoma, ER+/PR+/HER2-

reports.text: Specimen: left breast, 2 o'clock, ultrasound-guided 14-gauge core biopsy x4. Invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 2. Estrogen receptor positive (95%, strong). Progesterone receptor positive (70%, moderate). HER2 IHC 1+ (negative). Clip placed; post-procedure mammogram confirms clip at the biopsy site.
reports.conclusion: Left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2, ER positive, PR positive, HER2 negative (IHC 1+).

documents.title: Breast Surgery Consultation
documents.author: breast surgery
documents.body:
BREAST SURGERY CONSULTATION
Date: 03/31/2026
56-year-old woman with a 2.3 cm left breast mass at 2 o'clock on ultrasound found on screening; core biopsy shows invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2, ER+/PR+/HER2-negative. Axilla normal on ultrasound.
History: HFrEF (LVEF 35%, 1/2026), left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025, ruptured right MCA aneurysm coiled 11/2025, PE 11/2024, right frontal meningioma resected 5/2024, stage IA vulvar SCC excised 12/2023, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD. Mother had breast cancer at 62.
Medications: furosemide 40 mg daily, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: palpable firm mass in the left upper outer quadrant, mobile, with a small biopsy bruise. No skin changes. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes. Right breast normal.
Assessment: clinical T2 N0 left breast IDC, hormone receptor positive, HER2 negative.
Plan: left lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy. Cardiology and anesthesia input before surgery given her EF. Afterward, medical oncology and radiation oncology referrals; whole-breast radiation will follow lumpectomy. Surgery planned for 4/16.
Breast Surgery

events.reason: Left lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy

reports.text: A. Left breast, lumpectomy (oriented, clip present): invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 2, 2.4 cm. No lymphovascular invasion. documents.title: Recurrence score result
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — note to referring physicians
The 21-gene assay on Ms. Slattery's left breast IDC (pT2 N0, ER+/PR+/HER2-) returned a recurrence score of 31. In a postmenopausal woman with node-negative disease this score supports adjuvant chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy. I met with her and her son on 4/24 to review; she wishes to proceed. Because of her LVEF of 35% we will avoid anthracyclines and plan docetaxel/cyclophosphamide for 4 cycles. Port placement 4/30, cycle 1 on 5/7.
Medical Oncology

documents.title: Medical Oncology — Cycle 1
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — treatment visit, cycle 1 day 1
Date: 05/07/2026
Patient: Valerie Slattery, 56

Here to begin adjuvant chemotherapy for recently diagnosed left breast IDC, pT2 N0, stage IIA, grade 2, ER+/PR+/HER2-, recurrence score 31. Lumpectomy with SLNB 4/16 (3 weeks ago); right chest port placed 4/30 (1 week ago).
Other history: HFrEF (LVEF 35%, nonischemic), left atrial myxoma excised 5/2025, ruptured right MCA aneurysm coiled 11/2025, PE 11/2024 (completed anticoagulation), DVT 2021, right frontal meningioma resected 5/2024, stage IA vulvar SCC 12/2023, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD, GERD.
Medications: furosemide 40 mg daily, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits. Exam unremarkable apart from healing lumpectomy, axillary and port incisions without erythema.
Labs: hemoglobin 13.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 250, AST/ALT 20/22, bilirubin 0.8; renal function at her baseline.

Plan:
- Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 IV every 21 days x 4 cycles, given today. No anthracycline because of her ejection fraction.
- Pegfilgrastim on-body injector applied today.
- Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily for 3 days starting the day before each docetaxel dose (taken yesterday), for fluid retention and reactions. Expect higher sugars on those days.
- Ondansetron 8 mg every 8 hours as needed for nausea.
- Next cycle 5/28. Radiation oncology after chemotherapy, then endocrine therapy.
Medical Oncology

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (8 mg) by mouth twice daily for 3 days, starting the day before each docetaxel treatment

documents.title: Nausea and vomiting after cycle 1
documents.author: oncology RN
documents.body:
ONCOLOGY NURSE TELEPHONE NOTE (copy to PCP)
Ms. Slattery called this morning. Nausea started the day after cycle 1 and she vomited several times on days 2 through 4, worst on Saturday. Ondansetron helped for a few hours at a time. Now keeping down fluids and toast, urinating normally, no fever, no diarrhea. Weight per her log down a little, not dizzy on standing.
Reviewed with the oncologist: chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting after cycle 1. Plan olanzapine 5 mg at bedtime on days 1-4 starting with cycle 2, plus ondansetron as needed. Okay to skip furosemide on a day she cannot keep fluids down; call cardiology if weight rises. Call back if vomiting returns, unable to drink, or fever 100.4 or higher.
Oncology Nursing

Labs acceptable for treatment.

documents.title: Steroids and my sugar
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick question. The oncology nurse said my sugar was up on yesterday's labs and that it's from the dexamethasone. Should I be doing anything different with the metformin on those days? I feel fine and the nausea is much better this time.

documents.title: RE: Steroids and my sugar
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad this cycle is going better. Dexamethasone does raise blood sugar for a day or two around each treatment, and it settles once the doses are done. With only four cycles, no change to your metformin is needed. Drink plenty of water those days. We'll check your A1c at your June visit.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: MRI brain with and without contrast and time-of-flight MR angiography of the circle of Willis. Coil mass at the right MCA bifurcation with expected susceptibility artifact; no flow within the aneurysm sac and no neck remnant. Parent and branch vessels patent. Stable postoperative changes of right frontotemporal craniotomy with no nodular enhancement. No new parenchymal abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Stable, completely occluded coiled right MCA aneurysm without recanalization. No recurrent meningioma.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Check-in between cycles 2 and 3 of TC. Nausea controlled on olanzapine + ondansetron with cycle 2. Tired the first week after each cycle, then okay. Finished the school year on a reduced schedule.
MRI/MRA 6/11: coiled aneurysm stable, no recurrence of the meningioma.
HF: weights steady, no orthopnea, no edema. BMP with oncology labs each cycle.
Meds: furosemide 40 qAM, KCl 20, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, dexamethasone premed, ondansetron prn, olanzapine nights 1-4, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: weight down slightly. BP at goal. Port site clean. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P
1. Breast cancer, stage IIA — on adjuvant TC, cycle 3 on 6/18. Radiation to follow.
2. CINV — controlled with the added olanzapine.
3. T2DM — A1c running higher this year than in 2024-25, partly the steroid days; no change during chemo.
4. HFrEF — stable on furosemide/lisinopril. Renal function per oncology labs at baseline.
5. Hx SAH, meningioma — imaging reassuring.
RTC late August.

documents.author: medical oncology

MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — cycle 4 day 1 (final)
Date: 07/09/2026
Cycle 3 went smoothly; nausea controlled. Energy returns by the second week. No fever. No edema; weights stable per her log.
Medications unchanged. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: port clean. Lungs clear. No edema.
Labs acceptable.

documents.title: Radiation Oncology Consultation
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date: 07/23/2026
56-year-old with left breast IDC, pT2 N0, stage IIA, ER+/PR+/HER2-, after lumpectomy with negative margins and negative sentinel nodes (4/2026), and four cycles of docetaxel/cyclophosphamide completed 7/9. Nausea resolved since the last cycle.
Relevant history: HFrEF with LVEF 35%, left atrial myxoma excised 2025, coiled cerebral aneurysm 2025.
Medications: furosemide, potassium chloride, lisinopril, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: healed lumpectomy and axillary incisions, no seroma, full arm range of motion.
Recommendation: whole-breast radiation to the left breast, 40 Gy in 15 daily fractions. Deep-inspiration breath hold to keep the heart out of the field given her cardiac history. CT simulation next week; treatment to start 8/10. Endocrine therapy with letrozole after radiation per medical oncology.
Radiation Oncology
